notes:
Account summary: enterprise platform company building customer-facing AI agents and realtime personalization. Heavy emphasis on reliability; their SREs insist on deterministic tail latency for 99th pct tokens. Currently running mixed workload: streaming chat + nightly bulk embeddings + online reranking. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace brittle in-house GPU fleet. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees and documented failover behavior when pool is saturated.

Key quotes / highlights from last call: "We need to know what happens at 95% and 100% capacity — automatic model downgrade? cross-region shifts?"; "Can you commit to a per-route latency SLO and a deterministic CPU/GPU reservation model?".

Reliability & fallback priorities being evaluated: cross-region failover (primary region us-east, DR eu-west), model-variant fallback (quantized vs fp16), multi-tenant reserved GPU planning (pool sizing for baseline + burst), and explicit SLA language for RTO/RPO and traffic shedding. They want runbook examples and a failure-mode matrix.

POC details: 6-week dedicated evaluation with a reserved pool (8xA10 equivalent GPUs) + canary traffic split. POC goals: validate 99th pct request latency < 350ms for streaming chat at 1k concurrent users; embedding throughput 2000 qps with < 50ms mean token time; model variant fallback should maintain correctness within 5% eval metric delta.

Security/Compliance: need SAML SSO, SOC2 evidence, customer-managed KMS (HSM optional), audit logs exported to their SIEM, and optional on-prem bundle for regulatory tenant. Also asked about data residency enforcement and log retention windows.

Economic notes: prefer reserved commit for predictable unit cost; asked for pricing scenarios: steady-state vs seasonal spikes. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/kv-cache to lower per-token cost.

Tender/Procurement: procurement will push for SLA credits tied to latency/availability, not just uptime. Legal wants explicit language around cross-region failover time (target < 3 minutes for control-plane reconnection, < 10 minutes to rehydrate KV caches) and acceptable behavior during saturation (graceful degradation, prioritized routes).

Technical questions unresolved: how cross-region KV cache consistency is handled (cold-start penalty), whether model variant fallback preserves function calling behavior, and how pre-emption/eviction works with reserved pools. Also need a map of kernel/quantization compatibility for their chosen models.

Stubs/links: fireflies ff_20260117_3039 (product/architecture call), drive pricing deck (attached), Jira INF-7123 for preliminary infra questions.

Short-term next steps (from AE notes): deliver SLA draft with explicit RTO/RPO, share a 2-week POC runbook with load profile, provide cost model for reserved vs burst, organise SRE workshop (2-hour) to review failure-mode matrix.
